name: Giant Chocolate Chip Cookies
desc: Tessa Arias's quarter-pound cookies: cold butter, no chill, crisp edge and gooey middle

ingredients.raw: 3 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour (380 g plus the altitude bump)
ingredients.item: plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour (380 g plus the altitude bump)

ingredients.raw: 1 cup COLD unsalted butter, cubed (2 sticks / 227g, straight from fridge)
1 cup semisweet chocolate chunks, hand-chopped from a bar (reserve half for topping)
ingredients.item: semisweet chocolate chunks, hand-chopped from a bar (reserve half for topping)

ingredients.raw: 1 pinch flaky sea salt for finishing (optional but worth it)
ingredients.item: flaky sea salt for finishing (optional but worth it)

steps: Preheat and prep: Preheat oven to 375 F. Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper.
Whisk dry ingredients: In a medium bowl, whisk together 3 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon fine sea salt, 1 teaspoon baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon baking soda.

Beat cold butter and sugars: In the stand mixer, beat 1 cup COLD unsalted butter, cubed with 3/4 cup granulated sugar and 1 1/3 cups light brown sugar, packed on medium-high until well combined and fluffy. Cold butter takes longer than softened, expect 3 to 4 minutes . Do not swap in soft butter, cold is what keeps these thick.
Add eggs and vanilla: Add 2 large eggs one at a time, then 2 teaspoons vanilla extract, beating until combined.

Add flour and chocolate: Gradually beat in the flour mixture on low speed just until combined. Then beat in 1 1/2 cups semisweet chocolate chips and half of 1 cup semisweet chocolate chunks, hand-chopped from a bar.

Portion quarter-pound balls: Weigh out 113 g (4 oz) portions and roll into even balls. A scale beats the scoop here, this dough runs closer to 1/2 cup per 113 g. Place 6 per pan, spaced far apart. Press the reserved chunks from 1 cup semisweet chocolate chunks, hand-chopped from a bar into the tops.

Bake, longer for crispier: Bake 15 to 18 minutes  until edges are browned and cookies are puffy. You want crispy edges, so run toward the long end: check at 17, likely pull at 18 to 19 when the edge ring is properly golden brown. Less time = gooier, more time = crispier.
Salt and cool: Sprinkle with 1 pinch flaky sea salt for finishing immediately out of the oven. Cookies deflate slightly as they cool, that's normal. Let them set on the pan before moving.
